summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male nursing home resident with a history of cerebrovascular accident, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent urinary infections was admitted for suprapubic tenderness, abdominal distention, and fever. In the ER, his Foley catheter was found blocked and replaced, draining 800cc of cloudy urine. He was started on IV cefepime for suspected urosepsis. Blood cultures were negative, but urine culture grew Proteus, Klebsiella, and Morganella, all sensitive to ceftriaxone, prompting a switch in antibiotics. He developed right leg pain with a cool foot and absent pulse, initially concerning for ischemia, but vascular surgery attributed it to vasospasm given improvement and ongoing anticoagulation. The foot rewarmed and pulse returned. His G-tube became clogged and was successfully cleared by interventional radiology. His infection resolved, pain was controlled, and he was discharged to extended care on a 7-day course of IV ceftriaxone, with all home medications resumed including warfarin at 4mg daily.
